title: Batching

video.title: How to Batch (Almost) Any Cocktail | Serious Eats

keyPoints.line: every line by the same number.

read.bigIdea: A batch is the spec, multiplied.
read.where: Multiply **every ingredient** by the **number of drinks**: 2 oz × 20 = 40 oz. Keep **one unit** for the whole batch. Bitters scale too: count dashes, then measure them. Write the batch recipe down, pour one **test drink** and taste it against the single spec.
read.mixup: Don’t round one line and not the others. The balance moves.

video.title: Make Amazing Cocktails Fast | Pre-Batched Old Fashioned

keyPoints.line: one drink before and after: that’s the water.
needs a bit more; on ice, a bit less.

read.bigIdea: A batch has no ice, so the water goes in the bottle.
read.where: A stirred drink gets its water from the ice. A **pre-batched** stirred drink poured straight from the fridge doesn’t, so you **add the water** to the batch. Death & Co suggests about **20%** of the batch. The exact way: **weigh** one drink, stir it on ice, weigh it again; the difference is the water each drink needs. Drinks served **up** want a little more; drinks over **ice** a little less, since the ice keeps melting.
read.mixup: A batch that’s going to be stirred on ice again doesn’t get the water. It would end up double-diluted.

keyPoints.line: go in last, in the glass.

read.where: Spirits, liqueurs, vermouth and bitters keep well together. **Citrus** doesn’t: it fades within the day (Dave Arnold’s test), so add it at service or batch it that day. **Bubbles** (soda, sparkling wine) go flat: top each drink in the glass. **Egg** and **cream** need a hard shake to order.
read.mixup: A batched Martini keeps. A batched Margarita with yesterday’s lime doesn’t.

keyPoints.line: keep stirred batches in the fridge.
it at the top of each shift.

read.bigIdea: A batch is only as good as its label.
read.where: Every batch bottle gets the **drink name**, the **date** and **who made it**. Keep stirred batches **cold** so they pour ready to serve. **Taste** a batch at the start of each shift before the first drink goes out.
read.mixup: An unlabeled bottle on the bar is a guess. If it isn’t labeled, don’t pour it.

sources: Death & Co, “How to batch cocktails for a crowd” (fashioned.deathandcompany.com); Foodism, “Pre-batched cocktails” (foodism.co.uk); Cocktails Distilled, batching guide (cocktailsdistilled.com); Dave Arnold, “Fresh Lime Juice: WTF?”, Cooking Issues, Oct 1, 2010 (cookingissues.com). Checked Nov 8, 2026.
